observation: When an Opportunity is cloned, the cloned record's Opportunity Readiness is already marked as 'Approved' because it points to the original Opportunity Readiness record — user cannot delete and create a new one for the new opportunity
risk: Cloned Opportunities inherit an approved Readiness questionnaire that may not reflect the new deal's actual readiness; risk of inaccurate approval status for Expansions/Contract renewals
notes: BA confirmed: proceed with current behavior (cloned Opp Readiness stays approved). If different requirements arise for Expansions/Contract renewals, a new story will be created.

observation: POG Manager and POG Committee roles/profiles are not yet defined — no Profile, Permission Set Group, or role-based restrictions exist. Any user/role can currently be assigned as a POG Manager on the Opportunity Readiness record
risk: No access control around POG Manager and POG Committee approver assignments; unintended users could approve Opportunity Readiness; permissions will need to be reworked before production
notes: BA confirmed: proceed with MRD User permission as baseline to unblock dev/QA. Permissions rework planned for a future phase. Also impacts SF-666.

observation: User story SF-513 requires Country and State/Province picklist fields to be removed from the Lead object. However, the team decided in standup that full removal from the object is not necessary — hiding the fields from page layouts is sufficient. The Country field (Lookup type) still exists on the Lead object
risk: Fields remain on the object metadata and could be re-exposed on layouts accidentally; data could still be populated via API, imports, or automation even though hidden from the UI
notes: Discussed in standup: removal from object not necessary as per team — as long as field does not appear in the layout. Gabriel Fuoco confirmed the new Country field is a Lookup to the Country object. Pending final confirmation from BA/PO.

observation: Lookup and dropdown fields on page layouts are not context-filtered. For example, when adding a Legal Entity on an Account, the lookup shows all Account records instead of filtering to Legal Entity type only. This applies broadly across Account, Lead, and Opportunity objects where related record lookups or picklist values are not restricted by record type or context
risk: Users can accidentally select incorrect records (e.g. wrong account type); increases data entry errors; poor user experience with large unfiltered lists; potential data integrity issues in downstream systems
notes: Generic recommendation — not tied to a single Jira story. Affects multiple objects (Account, Lead, Opportunity). Recommend implementing filtered lookups and dependent picklists to restrict values by record type or context.

observation: Salesforce APIs accept invalid picklist values for restricted fields. For example, an Opportunity can be created via API with a Stage value outside the defined picklist options. This applies broadly across Account, Lead, and Opportunity objects — no server-side validation prevents invalid values being inserted through API calls
risk: Invalid data can enter the system via API, integrations (e.g. MuleSoft), or data loads, bypassing picklist restrictions enforced only at the UI level; leads to data integrity issues, broken reports, and downstream system errors
notes: Discussed in team meeting. Architect confirmed API is not exposed externally, so API testing is considered out of scope for MVP. However, internal integrations (MuleSoft, data loads) could still inject invalid values. Recommend adding Salesforce validation rules or Apex triggers to enforce picklist values at the data layer.

observation: Permission roles (Profiles, Permission Sets, Permission Set Groups) are not fully defined for all user personas across the Salesforce implementation. Testing is currently performed using baseline MRD User or Admin profiles rather than persona-specific permission configurations
risk: Cannot validate field-level security, object-level access, or feature visibility per persona; risk of over-privileged or under-privileged users in production; compliance and audit gaps; permission issues will only surface post-go-live
notes: Generic issue across the Salesforce implementation — not tied to a specific Jira story. Recommend defining Profiles, Permission Sets, and Permission Set Groups for each persona (e.g. Underwriter, MRD User, Operations, Finance) before UAT. Related to QA-002 (SF-676).

observation: Geography field on the Opportunity Readiness page does not save on the first attempt. User must navigate away and return to save it again for the value to persist. This is an out-of-the-box Salesforce platform issue that cannot be fixed by the development team
risk: Users may assume Geography was saved when it was not, leading to incomplete Opportunity Readiness records; creates confusion and extra manual steps; blocks automation of Opportunity Readiness workflows
notes: Out-of-the-box Salesforce platform bug — development team cannot fix directly. Development Lead needs to raise a support ticket with Salesforce to resolve. Workaround: save the record, return to it, and save Geography again.

observation: Account Status and Opportunity Status are tightly coupled in this implementation. BA confirmed that active accounts will only have one New Business opportunity (from initial onboarding), and after that only Expansion or Renewal opportunities. QA raised concern that this assumption may not be universally true — e.g. edge cases where multiple New Business opportunities exist for an account, or where opportunity status transitions don't align with account status
risk: If the one-New-Business-per-account assumption does not hold for all scenarios, status-driven automation, workflows, and validations could produce incorrect results; account lifecycle reporting may be inaccurate; edge cases could surface in production with no handling
notes: BA (Abby) confirmed: 'There are no new business opportunities for existing active accounts. Active accounts will have one New Business opportunity for when they were onboarded. After that, only Expansions or Renewals.' QA proceeding with this assumption for MVP. Recommend revisiting if business model evolves or edge cases are reported.

observation: The 'Submit for Approval' button remains visible and clickable on the Opportunity Readiness page even after all approvals have been completed. Users can re-submit an already fully approved record
risk: Confusing UX — users may accidentally re-trigger the approval process on an already approved record; however, does not block functionality or allow disallowed processes
notes: PO confirmed: not a bug. Does not block functionality nor allow disallowed processes. Can be enhanced later to hide/disable the button post-approval. Closing as accepted for MVP.

observation: All 'details' fields across multiple objects (Account, Opportunity, Opportunity Readiness, etc.) accept a single dot '.' or any minimal character as a valid value. There is no minimum word count, character length, or meaningful content validation on these fields despite their labels implying substantive input is expected
risk: Users can bypass mandatory-feeling fields with trivial input (e.g. '.'), resulting in incomplete records; downstream processes relying on details fields will have no meaningful data; audit and compliance gaps where detail is required
notes: No clear answer from BA or PO on what minimum input requirements should be for details fields. Recommend defining validation rules (e.g. minimum character count, regex patterns) for all free-text 'details' fields across objects. Awaiting PO decision.

observation: The Insurance Carrier lookup field on the Account does not filter by Account Type. When searching for an insurance carrier, all accounts are listed regardless of type. Only accounts with Account Type 'Insurer' should appear in the Insurance Carrier lookup results
risk: Users can select a non-Insurer account as the Insurance Carrier, leading to incorrect data associations; downstream processes and reports relying on Insurance Carrier will reference wrong account types
notes: QA raised in SF-646 comments. PO acknowledged it would be good to have the Insurer type filter but not blocking for MVP. Recommend implementing a filtered lookup to restrict Insurance Carrier field to Insurer-type accounts only. Related to QA-004 (generic lookup filtering gap).

observation: The Underwriter Review data capture implementation uses shortened field labels compared to what was specified in the Excel sheet attached to the SF-358 requirement. The functionality is the same but the labels in the UI do not match the original specification
risk: Cosmetic — labels shortened but functionality intact. However, discrepancy between spec and implementation could cause confusion during UAT, user training, and documentation if not formally acknowledged
notes: QA raised the label discrepancy with PO — awaiting confirmation on whether shortened labels are acceptable or should be updated to match the original Excel specification. No clear response yet.

observation: When an Opportunity's type is changed from 'New Business' to another type (e.g. Expansion, Renewal), the associated Opportunity Readiness record is not removed. The system currently allows users to change the Opportunity type freely, leaving an orphaned Readiness record that was only relevant for New Business
risk: Orphaned Opportunity Readiness records on non-New Business opportunities; data integrity issues; Readiness approval status may be misinterpreted for Expansion/Renewal opportunities where it does not apply
notes: Bug SF-906 cancelled. Team decided to raise a new user story (SF-899) to restrict users from changing Opportunity type instead. SF-899 will come in a future phase. Until then, Opportunity type can still be changed and orphaned Readiness records may exist.

observation: (1) Scenario-2 fails: Duplicate pairing — same member–legal entity account combination is accepted when it should not be. (2) Entity relationships are not grouped by Legal Entity and Group; they appear in a flat list instead.
risk: Duplicate member–legal entity relationships can be created; grouped display for Legal Entity/Group views is not available.
notes: BA (Abby Parker) confirmed: 'it is okay as it is.' Manikantan to proceed. Both duplicate pairing acceptance and non-grouped display are accepted as known limitations for MVP Phase 1.

observation: SF-883: 'Updated Commission Rate' currently accepts 0.00 as a valid value. Tomos Rands (PO) indicated this is acceptable for MVP—relying on MRDs not to misuse zero inappropriately. Separately, the written acceptance criteria include Scenario 2: when a Rate & Commission Changes Opportunity exists and 'Updated Commission Rate' is blank, the MRD's save must be prevented—i.e. validation is required before save.
risk: If blank (or edge cases around zero vs blank) is not enforced as per Scenario 2, opportunities could be saved without a proper Updated Commission Rate, conflicting with the documented requirement and weakening data quality for commission data.
notes: PO position (Tomos Rands): trusting MRDs on 0.00 is fine for MVP. QA documenting explicit requirement text for traceability: 'Scenario 2: Updated Commission Rate is required before saving — Given a Rate & Commission Changes Opportunity exists and Updated Commission Rate is blank, When the MRD attempts to save the Opportunity, Then the save must be prevented.' Align future validation work (blank vs 0.00) with BA/PO if Scenario 2 must be fully automated in a later phase.

observation: SF-748: Contact name components Title, MiddleName, and Suffix from Salesforce do not appear in Dataverse after sync — middlename, salutation, and suffix stay NULL while firstname/lastname populate; fullname omits middle and suffix. QA expected alignment with mapping doc tab "I contacts -> externalcontact" (Salesforce: FirstName, LastName, MiddleName, Title, Suffix → Dynamics: firstname, lastname, middlename, salutation, suffix). Example Salesforce name "Mr. Int FirstName Int Mid Int Last Sr" reproduced the gap in DB.
risk: Anyone relying on Dataverse for a full legal/salutation-style contact name will see incomplete data versus Salesforce; traceability gap between integration mapping documentation and MVP field scope.
notes: BA (Abby Long): In Dataverse UI, contact shows only First Name, Last Name, Email, and related Party — not salutation, suffix, or middle name. Backend NULLs reflect that this information is not captured in the minimal Salesforce→Dataverse set for contacts. Contacts are ancillary; users who need full detail should use Salesforce. Discussion with Ana: no strong MVP requirement to sync all name components when those fields are not surfaced in Dataverse UI.

observation: SF-977 — Scenario "Create Draft - Product Expansion": Given an Actuary creates a Product_Map__c record related to an Opportunity with Type = "Expansion", when the record is saved, acceptance criteria had implied Product Map Status would be set to "Draft - Product Expansion". Per product clarification, that status is **not** auto-set; the user must select the appropriate status (it does not default to Draft - Product Expansion for Expansion opportunities). Related work: SF-958 (Update Product Mapping Status Picklist Values); in refinement the effort to implement the last two scenarios was considered high and those scenarios were omitted from delivery.
risk: Automated tests or Gherkin may still expect an auto-default to "Draft - Product Expansion" and report false failures until aligned with the agreed behavior. Risk of confusion between historical AC text and current product rules (e.g. Draft availability for Expansion).
notes: Abby: "The status does not need to default to draft- product expansion for expansion opportunities. We did have some requirements in SF-958: Update Product Mapping Status Picklist Values — however when we were in refinement the effort to implement the last two scenarios was high so we opted to leave them out. I can see in the above comments that Gabriel has blocked Draft from being chosen for Expansion opportunities so I think that okay."

observation: SF-1217: When creating an External Contact in Salesforce, the Account field is mandatory on the page layout. QA observed that some existing Dynamics 365 contact records have no Party value populated (see screenshot attached to SF-1217 — Salesforce New Contact form shows Account required; Dynamics Active Contacts list shows empty Party column). Question raised: is Account mandatory for external contact, and will migration fail for records missing Party in Dataverse?
risk: Contacts migrated from Dataverse without a Party (Account) association may not meet Salesforce UI requirements for manual management; data cleanup may be needed before or after migration for orphaned contacts.
notes: BA (Abby Parker): The Account field should be mandatory when creating a Contact via the UI — enforced by page layout only. API creation and migration do not enforce mandatory Account. For Dataverse records with no Account/Party, BA will work to populate those values so they can be managed in Salesforce. Bug can be closed.
